messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — elevated 5xx rate for Stripe webhook delivery to /events: 429 and 503 spikes. Alerting oncall and creating thread (id=inc_2026_03_12).

marta (oncall): paging @josh @kevin — I'm looking at delivery failures, lots of 429s from Stripe (rate_limit). Can someone jump in?

josh: on it. I see a surge starting ~00:04 UTC, upstream responses showing X-RateLimit-Limit header low and X-RateLimit-Remaining dropping to 0. Sample log: ```2026-03-12T00:06:12Z POST /events 429  body: {"error":"rate_limited"} headers: {"x-ratelimit-limit":"100","x-ratelimit-remaining":"0","retry-after":"30"}```

kevin: I'm with you. Looks like Stripe is applying stricter quota enforcement for our integration key — possibly due to billing/entitlement mismatch. Support ticket says queued webhooks delivery is delayed.

marta (oncall): quick customer-impact check — which features rely on immediate webhook delivery? @customer-success?

customer-success: Affected: invoice payment success notifications, subscription state updates that drive access provisioning. Currently seeing some customers reporting delayed account activation. Severity: user-visible but intermittent. We'll prepare comms if this persists beyond 2h.

josh: mitigation options I can run now: 1) switch to polling fallback for account provisioning (temporary) 2) enable exponential backoff + increase retry window on our webhook worker 3) disable noncritical webhook event types to reduce volume. Which do we want to prioritize?

kevin: also open question: are we hitting per-key TPS limits or aggregate across endpoints? Stripe's headers point to per-key. We should rotate to a secondary webhook signing key / integration ID if available, or throttle outgoing to match their rate hints.

sara: Ops can spin up polling workers for subscription status and invoice checks. I can deploy a small job that polls Stripe payment intents for pending accounts every 30s for the next 4 hours. That avoids reliance on webhooks for provisioning.

marta (oncall): OK plan: 1) immediate — enable polling fallback (sara) 2) josh — patch webhook worker to respect Retry-After and increase queue retry window + reduce concurrency to 10% to stop hard-failing messages 3) kevin — contact Stripe support and escalate, include tenant examples and rate-limit headers 4) customer-success prepare short customer notice if >1h unresolved.

josh: patching now. Code snippet I'm deploying: ```// respect retry-after
if (resp.status === 429) { const wait = parseInt(resp.headers['retry-after'] || '5'); await sleep(wait * 1000); retry(); }
// reduce parallelism
worker.poolSize = Math.max(1, Math.floor(worker.poolSize * 0.1));``` Deploying to canary 1/3 traffic.

ops-bot: deploy started by josh to canary (deploy/6789). Logs stream URL: https://ci.internal/reports/deploy/6789

kevin: Stripe support replied — they see rate-limit enforcement on our webhook key due to an account-level billing flag. They've queued a manual review but ETA unknown ("investigation in progress"). Suggested best-effort: stagger retries and lower throughput. They've provided a temporary increase option but requires account admin confirmation. Raising this to support-ops.

support-ops: I've initiated the admin auth flow for the temporary increase and added billing contact cc. Ticket: https://support.stripe.com/tickets/29384. Also requested log export for our traffic spike window.

sara: Polling workers deployed. Status: job started, hitting Stripe API with idempotent GETs for invoice/subscription states at 30s interval for flagged accounts. Minimal rate impact; we limited to 100 reqs/min across all pollers.

josh: Canary patch live. Worker concurrency reduced, retry window to 24h for transient failures, and we've suppressed nonessential events (webhook filter config updated). We still have a backlog in SQS of ~12k webhooks. Working through the queue slowly at reduced concurrency to avoid re-triggering rate limits.

marta (oncall): Customer impact update: queues draining slower but service access restore is happening for many customers via polling. CS seeing fewer new tickets. Continue throttled drain. If Stripe doesn't restore within 3h we move to plan B: temporary manual provisioning via support-ops for urgent customers.

kevin: Stripe replied again — still investigating; no ETA. They acknowledged increased rate enforcement and suggested we reduce spikes / use multiple webhook endpoints per account. They're also giving us a 2x temporary soft-limit tweak if account admin accepts. support-ops — can you authorize?

support-ops: Admin confirmed and accepted the temporary increase. Stripe applied a soft bump. Monitoring shows X-RateLimit-Remaining recovering slowly.

ops-bot: alert suppression applied for the incident channel per marta request (suppressed 30m)

josh: Backlog processing rate increased safely, no new 429s for the last 5 minutes. Metrics: webhook success rate up from 68% -> 96% on canary, now rolling to remaining workers.

customer-success: Seeing account activations catch up. We'll send a brief status note to affected customers summarizing cause (Stripe rate enforcement) and mitigation (polling fallback, temporary rate bump). Draft ready for review.

marta (oncall): Next steps: 1) keep throttled queue drain until fully cleared 2) get postmortem with root cause (billing/account flag + traffic pattern) 3) run a stress test of webhook traffic patterns against Stripe soft-limits before next major release 4) follow-up with billing team on entitlement alignment. I'll convert this thread to a postmortem doc after resolution. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
